I had the most interesting and unique experience at the Stanford Deep Tech Hackathon with Arshia Bhattacharyya and Manya Saxena . We registered for the event on Luma and had valid tickets. However, since we arrived late, we were told by the security guard that we could no longer enter the venue. Making use of the persistence and communication skills I gained through the door-to-door sales internship I had earlier this summer, I tried negotiating with the security guards and the organizers more than five times. Unfortunately, every answer we got was no. However, we never gave up and decided to make the most of the opportunity. (We even debated whether we should just go home or hang around the Stanford campus for a while though lol) Eventually, we decided to join the hackathon through the virtual track provided for participants who lived far away. We worked from a bench outside the venue and kept hacking until 7 pm, even after many people had gone home. What we built was Smoke Signal, a personalized wildfire risk assessment platform that helps commuters make safer travel decisions using real-time satellite, wildfire, and weather data. Instead of requiring users to interpret multiple data sources themselves, our AI provides personalized risk assessments based on their destination and current conditions. Using NASA satellite imagery, wildfire reports, and real-time weather data, Smoke Signal helps users make safer and faster travel decisions. 🎥 Pitch: https://lnkd.in/gwHfWMqc 🎥 Demo: https://lnkd.in/gUvKVbcr We're getting the results in two weeks, so fingers crossed, and we'll bring home the $5K in Google Cloud credits! Most importantly, I'm grateful we didn't let a setback stop us from building something meaningful. Sometimes the best part of a hackathon isn't where you work, it's that you keep building. Huge thanks to Daniel Goncharov for the invitation, and to Google DeepMind and Replit for supporting such an awesome event. ...more

We’re excited to introduce VentEase. Our mission is to tackle a major challenge in intensive care: surgical patients who struggle to wean from mechanical ventilation. VentEase is developing a catheter-based phrenic nerve stimulation system designed to keep the diaphragm active during ventilation, with the goal of shortening weaning time and reducing complications such as ventilator-associated pneumonia. Born out of the Japan Biodesign at Osaka University, we’re committed to turning unmet clinical needs into practical solutions for patients, clinicians, and hospitals worldwide. Thank you for following our journey. ...more ...more

WHO THE FREAK LET ME INTO BERKELEY!?!!?!?!?!? I’m currently sitting on the flight to San Francisco, and I genuinely don’t know how to process the fact that I’m actually on my way to UC Berkeley, which was ranked as the Top 7th University in the world. ( https://lnkd.in/e5pTSfWR ) A few months ago, I was just applying for an exchange and hoping for the best. I applied across the world to around five universities. Somehow, I ended up being selected as the only University of Auckland student for Berkeley’s 2026 Fall exchange programme. I’m feeling a pretty ridiculous mix of excitement, nerves and disbelief. I’m going to miss Auckland and everyone back home, but I’m also incredibly excited to see what the next few months bring. See yall soon! 🇺🇸🐻

I visited my father's grave today. ❤️‍🩹 今日、父のお墓参りに行きました。 He was a great man who served society. He also noticed the smallest things, at home and in us. When I was only 18, he gave his life to save a drunk driver he saw crash on the highway. Losing him was very difficult and affected my health in ways I didn't understand for a long time, as I sealed away my emotions to work and study desperately to survive. But I have come a long way since then. I was fortunate to meet people who cared for me like family, especially in Japan and the Bay Area. I would not be where I am today without their kindness. Much of my desire to help society began with my father. I hope that through my work and the way I care for others, I can carry forward what he taught me. Now an adult on the path of healing, I am working to re-develop that deep attentiveness my dad had while he was alive. Thank you, Papa. And thank you to everyone who is helping me find my way. 🙏

A couple of months ago we handed in a semester paper with two sources that did not exist. We had used AI to pull the literature together and we trusted what came back. Our professors found them. We admitted it the same day and barely passed the subject. Once the panic wore off, we went looking for the tool that would have kept us honest, and there wasn't one. So we started building it. First for ourselves, then for the students we interviewed, who turned out to carry the same fear we did. The next semester we wrote our master's thesis inside it. Since then we have worked together with a small group of students testing the product and receiving feedback. That part is nearly over. We are close to making Skriptr available to every student. Skriptr raises the bar for what students can achieve, instead of lowering it for what they can skip. The whole story is on our About page, link in the comment section.
